notes.title: Kabounce Patch 1.37
notes.notes:
Hi everyone,

We rolled out another patch to hotfix a few reported issues.

[h1]HOTFIXES[/h1]
[list]
[*] Fixed a wrong connection between Rhythm and Ascend causing the progression between levels to be incorrect
[*] Average statistics in Ranked matches now display correctly instead of accumulating
[*] The number in the unlock screen now represents the total lootballs instead of just the ones in the machine
[*] Fixed Sol feat of strength not having an icon/description when unlocking
[/list]

[h1]IMPROVEMENTS[/h1]
[list]
[*] Your own player icon in the end of match screen, or those of split screen players, are now visually distinct from other players when pressing rematch
[*] Player that leave at the end of a match receive a visually distinct icon in the end of match screen
[/list]

[list]
[*] In ranked matches, you should no longer get stuck in the respawn tube

Let us know if you encounter any other issues on the Steam Discussion boards, contact us through Discord or support@stitchheads.com.

-Stitch Heads

notes.title: Server Status Report
notes.notes:
Hi everyone!

We received reports of players experiencing lag and high ping.

Certain matchmaking settings preferred to put players in a server with other people - even outside your own region. We've made some more changes that will keep players in their own region when the server settings are set to 'auto'. We've also been testing the optimal capacity per server even more.

Cheers,

notes.title: October Update News
notes.notes:
October 25 we’re launching a new [b]update, and free weekend![/b] In this post I want to detail some of the upcoming plans.

What to expect in the mysteriously-ambiguously-titled [spoiler]Halloween[/spoiler] update:
[list]
[*]New [spoiler]Halloween[/spoiler] Skins
[*]New Challenge Levels
[*]The real speedsters and leaderboard fanatics will be able to earn a [b]Blue star[/b] in challenges! 
[*]Kabounce will have Rich Presence support on Discord, invite players to a party via Discord directly ([url=discord.gg/kabounce]and shamelessly join ours here[/url]) - or see what friends are up to in Kabounce
[/list]

We’ll also start dropping some sneak peeks for the new customization in the coming weeks.

[h1]What's next for Kabounce?[/h1]
In December we have something much bigger planned, we’re really excited to share it – unfortunately we can’t – yet! Not being mean here, you may feel it is, and maybe it's a little cruel, but it's definitely not mean... Okay: once we're able to share and the time is right, we’ll update the community. Additionally, as usual, also expect extra content to roll out in December, the theme is still super secretive.

[h1]What else are we working on?[/h1]
We’re working on a range of things, experimenting with new game modes and content that is too early to share. During these stages plans and content tends to evolve dramatically. Sharing would be very mean if we end up exciting you only to change it later, and we just discussed this - we're not mean. 

If we feel the quality of the new content is heading in the right direction and up to the standard we want, we can start sharing more details.

[h1]Frequent Question[/h1]
One of the dominant questions players in our community have wondered is: are we going to support [b]other platforms/consoles or additional stores?[/b].

We're laser focused right now and once we're able to share anything new we will schedule a press release and update our community of any important information.

I’m sorry I have to be vague on some matters, some of this is also meant to assure you that we are still working on Kabounce and that we aren’t dropping support, and to ensure we can roll out an effective news-worthy promotion for any future plans we may have.

notes.title: Post Kabounce Beta
notes.notes:
Hi!

With the beta having ended last Monday, we've been incredibly busy compiling all the feedback, bug reports, and answering community questions.

We'd sincerely like to thank the group of players we selected from all over the world that had a chance to play the beta for their efforts in reporting feedback and bugs to us. The majority of you were from the EU and US, we even had a few from South America, China and Australia join in - however, we did not have any server presence there.

[h1]Our first post-beta steps[/h1]
We've noticed some people had difficulties with the initial training stages, while others breezed through it. We've come up with some solutions that we believe will work for both ends of the spectrum and have already started on implementation. 

We've already fixed several bugs, including some minor bugs with the ghosts and stats. The experience curve is being adjusted to more smoothly progress players from level to level, and we're improving the translations that were missing.

We've also taken note of any mouse controls that can still be improved, the group system on Steam, and any networking issues that were present.

In general, we're adding some quality of life improvements such as leaderboards that can be viewed within the challenges and a player score overlay option during multiplayer matches. This will make it easier to see players in a match and how they rank. 

This is not everything we have in the pipeline, but we will share more as it becomes available.

[h1]What will be added at launch[/h1]
[list]
[*][b]Custom Match:[/b] (disabled during beta) allows you to select any multiplayer map and create a private match, hosted by the group leader. You can add bots, set difficulty and maximum game size.
[*][b]Challenges:[/b] More challenges will be available in release, we have around 20-21 done and a few more in development, aiming for 30.
[*][b]Multiplayer Challenges:[/b] (was disabled during beta) play challenges casually with friends, or race each other for the best time. Group leader hosts.
[*][b]Customization:[/b] More customization will be available at launch. We haven't shown everything yet ;)
[*][b]Multiplayer Levels:[/b] Two more multiplayer maps are nearly done. We'll show more once the artists have completed their art passes of the levels.
[*][b]Achievements:[/b] While these weren't really available during the beta, we made sure you could still unlock them in-game, just not on Steam. We've already adjusted the rewards to more accurately represent the difficulty in obtaining each achievement.
[/list]

Thank you for reading, we truly hope everyone enjoyed the beta. Any feedback is always welcome and we'll continue to polish up the game. Sit tight for the announcement on our release date.

-Tim

notes.title: Kabounce Pinball Customisation
notes.notes:
[h1]Kabounce customisations[/h1]
This weekend our artists provide a sneak peek into some of the Customisation available in Kabounce. [b]Note: all Customisation is cosmetic only, these only affect how your pinball looks[/b].
[img]https://i.imgur.com/ftnqZCJ.gif[/img]

Initially, we already had plans for a Customisation system in Kabounce; however, you could only pick a pinball and trail. This wasn’t really sufficient, we had the ambition for more! The Customisation started with one of the artists adding a top hat, monocle, and moustache to a pinball – we were sold, it sparked creativity in all of us. 

Originally we thought, there is only so much we can do with balls [spheres], right? Wrong! We expanded the range of Customisation options to include more hats, glasses, bowties, moustaches, arms, wings and much, much more (ridiculous) additions! 

[h1]Pinballs need categories:[/h1]
To keep our database of items structured (and selectable for players) we categorised everything: 
[List]
[*][B]Base:[/b] the Pinball which is the cute, the bad and the weird (sometimes expressed as a single ball)
[*][b]Modification:[/b] materials or paint jobs for your Pinball.
[*][b]Trails:[/b] leave a dash of magic behind, or party it up with some confetti.
[*][B]Top Accessories:[/b] hats, horns and other oddities. These can even be rotated and tilted for a perfect fit.
[*][b]Middle Accessories:[/b] glasses, goggles, shades and other blinkers
[*][b]Special Accessories:[/b] these add a lot of variation and are often placed around the sides, bottom or backside of the pinball. Including (but not limited to) unique selections such as wings, arms, side wheels, ties or noses.
[/list]
If you’ve slapped on all the parts, you either have a cute or badass pinball – or your own personal meme.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/DOqAEFO.gif[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/jKCG0HC.gif[/img]

[h1]Rarities[/h1]
To separate the complexity and impressiveness of the Customisation options we categorised them into rarities, these are: Common, Rare, Epic and Legendary. Common items in general are simpler, such as caps and top hats, whereas legendary cosmetics can be fully animated assets! Collect all the legendaries and show your friends who’s the true pinball wizard!

[h1]To roll or not to roll[/h1]
Making these Pinballs is sometimes hard as… well… balls. When we added eyes and more character to the pinballs, we ran into some difficulties with the accessories, it really didn’t look good to see a hat at a relative height above;  while the Pinball (with eyes) rolls around. For this reason we made several internal variations or types of Pinballs to aid our development .

Normal Pinballs are those with simply a texture or a flavour skin/effect, these will always roll normally, hats will float above, glasses are attached to their front, but stay in place – to give a sense of direction.

The animated Pinballs were a lot tougher, they have a clear front and forward – mostly because of their eyes - in some cases we simply keep their eyes in the direction you’re rolling at all times. This makes it feel much more readable in which direction they are going, and accessories fit plus look better.

In more extreme cases we wanted to keep the rolling effect, eyes included, but not have the accessory meaninglessly float above. To avoid accessories which are rolling with the ball clipping too much through other objects (accessories don’t have collision which is a gameplay oriented decision), we scaled down a lot of the accessories for those specific cases so they still work with the animated Pinballs.

We’ve seen so many weird Pinball dress ups we could have started a YouTube series, but in the end we didn’t want to have the Pinball roll and stop only to be looking into the bottom of a hat, or faceplanted on the floor with a hat on its metallic butt.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/SEB4pFg.gif[/img]

We look forward to find out what YOU can create!
-Joris, Kim, Laura and Robbie

[b]Find daily tweets [url=www.twitter.com/StitchHeads]on our twitter[/url] or search #pinballoftheday . We showcase a new customisation set each day![/b]

[i]Drop by on Discord where you can usually find us dwelling and have a chat!
http://discord.gg/Kabounce

You can also help us by sharing this blog to your friends or the world.[/i]

P.S.
Here are some of our favourite combinations:

To separate the complexity and impressiveness of the Customisation options we categorised them into rarities, these are: Common, Rare, Epic and Legendary. Common items in general are simpler, such as caps and top hats, whereas legendary cosmetics can be fully animated assets! Collect all the legendaries and show your friends who’s the true pinball wizard!

[h1]To roll or not to roll[/h1]
Making these Pinballs is sometimes hard as… well… balls. When we added eyes and more character to the pinballs, we ran into some difficulties with the accessories, it really didn’t look good to see a hat at a relative height above;  while the Pinball (with eyes) rolls around. For this reason we made several internal variations or types of Pinballs to aid our development .

Normal Pinballs are those with simply a texture or a flavour skin/effect, these will always roll normally, hats will float above, glasses are attached to their front, but stay in place – to give a sense of direction.

The animated Pinballs were a lot tougher, they have a clear front and forward – mostly because of their eyes - in some cases we simply keep their eyes in the direction you’re rolling at all times. This makes it feel much more readable in which direction they are going, and accessories fit plus look better.

In more extreme cases we wanted to keep the rolling effect, eyes included, but not have the accessory meaninglessly float above. notes.title: Kabounce Map Design
notes.notes:
How do we design spaces for Kabounce’s unique gameplay and movement? This weekend it’s time to talk [b]map design[/b]!
[img]https://i.imgur.com/RLYf18k.gif[/img]
An important aspect in Kabounce Multiplayer is that the playing field itself is a big part of the objective. It’s all about capturing as many Bumpers and Hoops as possible.

[h1]Rolling, bouncing, and platforming[/h1]
Designing a Multiplayer map comes down to balancing the rolling and bouncing on the ground with the aerial platforming routes. 
On the ground you’ll mainly find Bumpers, which play a big role in a team’s overall domination of the playing field. They are super dynamic, Clusters of Bumpers can be used to quickly increase speed, get combo, and charge your abilities.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/DciLtUQ.gif[/img]
You can also jump on top of a Bumper or use Hoops to keep yourself in the air. Hoops give a boost, which allows you to quickly traverse the map. With a well-timed Jump or Dash you can use it to launch yourself to great heights! Platforming through the air can give you a lot of points, makes it harder for opponents to eliminate you, and gives you an advantageous overview to plan your offensive manoeuvres.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/QDAwoPo.gif[/img]
At first it can be quite difficult to keep yourself in the air, but once you start mastering the movement, you’ll be able to fly around the map like a super pinball!
[img]https://i.imgur.com/BQRnPIH.gif[/img]
While doing aerial platforming, you won’t be able to build your combo or charge your abilities as fast – so you’ll want to capture the clusters on the ground too!

[h1]Map ‘flow’[/h1]
[b]Flow[/b] is a word that is often used to describe the invisible driving force that guides you and allows you to constantly keep moving, whilst making interesting decisions along the way. It makes a map “feel” good and fun to play.

The flow of Kabounce’s gameplay is very dynamic. As a Designer it becomes less about designing paths that go in a specific direction, and more about placing Bumpers and Hoops in such a way that they can be linked up from many different angles. This allows you to keep the Pinball’s momentum going at all times, whilst choosing between different options on the fly.

With every map we try to create a layout that provides a different balance and a different set of options. 

There is a lot more that goes into creating a Multiplayer map for Kabounce, but hopefully this gives some interesting insights into our map development!

Thanks for reading! Share your thoughts in the comment section below.
-Mart

notes.title: Kabounce Camera System
notes.notes:
So… you’re controlling a pinball in third person, bouncing around and you can rapidly change direction or speed with spinning, powersliding, dashing – how is this not barf simulator 8000? Let’s talk about the camera.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/SOoDCB1.gif[/img] 

[h1]Camera Design Pillar[/h1]
A very important topic for us has always been the camera. Most third person games have it as a common enemy, it’s a lot of work to get right. The camera can also influence a player's wellbeing, some people are more easily jarred by camera movement than others, but there are games that can be nauseating. Because our game is so frantic, we took extra care to develop the camera system until we stopped hearing or noticing complaints of discomfort.

We felt it was incredibly important that you didn’t need to control the camera. We designed a smart system that would react to most situations and give you the necessary overview; however, if needed you can take back control from the automated system at any time.

While covering all the exact details is a much too extensive topic, in essence our camera system checks a for a range of elements: your distance from the ground, speed, input, what you hit, your turn rate, and your proximity to objects amongst things.

[h1]Default & Bumper Camera[/h1]
The default camera follows the player as they move with a slight delay and spring – making it feel more dynamic. Additionally, a bumper camera state becomes active for a split second when you hit a bumper, it ensures that multiple consecutive hits don’t actually make your brain feel that you’re just gone trough a pinball machine… Without this, we noticed it wasn’t very comfortable to look at!
[img]https://i.imgur.com/p2hafP9.gif[/img]

[h1]Air Camera[/h1]
To keep combat and platforming options in mind, the camera adjusts when you go high/vertical in Kabounce. The primary necessity at this point is to give players more overview, therefore the camera zooms out and slightly pitches downwards. This happens very gradually, and isn’t that noticeable until you compare rolling on the ground to being in the air.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/aXtYsAa.gif[/img]

[h1]Camera Control[/h1]
If needed, players can change the camera orientation at any point – this also helps tremendously with targeting your abilities.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/nFMLfcs.gif[/img]

[h1]Player Targeting Camera[/h1]
Sometimes you just want to focus on the movement, but still focus a target, for this purpose we have a ‘Player Targeting Camera’ selecting a player closest in view; however, you can cycle through targets or disable it at any time.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/jUoQ1eP.gif[/img]

[h1]Feedback[/h1]
We try to make sure all our camera feedback is complimentary and subtle - but it is a fantastic tool to give feedback to players, whether it is camera shakes, field of view changes on speed, particles or a blur.  All this feedback can of course be disabled from the settings menu.

[h1]Special Cases[/h1]
Some cases are special, and no smart system really felt good enough for it. For these specific cases we added a custom camera to take over whenever the situation arises. For example, when going through half pipes or finishing a challenge.

Thanks for reading! Share your thoughts in the comment section below. We’ll be back next weekend with more Kabounce features!
-Tim

notes.title: C-C-C-COMBO! feature preview
notes.notes:
Another weekend, another series! The fourth blog will cover our [b]Combo[/b] system.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/lnUWpjP.gif[/img] 
[h1]Combos & Points[/h1]
In Kabounce your main objective is to accumulate points, your [b]Combo[/b] grants a bonus point multiplier, and thus the opportunity to exponentially increase the points you gain. Staying in a good combo flow is important to gain an advantage, but it becomes increasingly difficult when players try to eliminate you, or when you’re trying to stop someone else.

More so, if you have an awesome combo going, and the goal opens (more on the goal in a different blog), you need to make a choice: bank or continue racking up combo? The more combo and points you gather, the more you are at risk from being targeted by opposing player and have a portion of your points stolen.

The real power of playing well with the combo comes from doing meaningful actions in the game so you maximize points. The higher the combo, the higher the multiplier. Similarly, the more points you gain during your combo, the higher the bonus. Try to build up a combo, and eliminate a player within your combo to receive a sweet, sweet point payout.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/bhFrO1O.gif[/img]

Be sure to watch out when carrying points and not scoring though, you’ll lose your points just as easily if you’re rolling around as a glorified profit target.
One strategy is to rack up a combo when your points are still low, racking up a high combo fast puts you in a vulnerable position - bouncing around in a cluster of bumpers – you’re an easy target. Once your combo multiplier is high enough, try to eliminate a player and profit! 

There’s much more to points and combo strategies, but we’ll leave it at this – we’re not going to spoil everything!

Thanks for reading! Share your thoughts in the comment section below.

notes.title: Kabounce Dev Blog - Movement Part 3
notes.notes:
In this third blog of the series we’d like to reveal the [b]Powerslide[/b] movement mechanic, which is mostly meant for those speedsters amongst you.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/bPIdpdT.gif[/img] 

[h1]Powerslide[/h1]
The [b]Powerslide[/b] has had its own iterative process to become a version most fitting Kabounce. Though, the base of it has been persistent throughout: converting speed on the ground into changing direction in a smoothly curved motion. This base is what we call [b]Drift[/b].

What we felt missing, was a ‘punch’, something to make it truly worthwhile. This is how the boost that comes with the [b]Powerslide[/b] was born. The provided speed bonus and the juiciness* of a good execution make it more Kabounce-esque. Especially in challenges is where its agile application comes to full appreciation, as you can use it to quickly pass a corner after landing with a [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/431930/announcements/detail/1674648628976245782][b]Spin[/b][/url].

[i]* Juiciness is a term we use in game development to describe multiple layers of positive feedback to satisfy user-input… It’s essentially an adjective for “woa that was pretty cool”.[/i]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/SYbmFpF.gif[/img] 

[h1]Slingshot[/h1]
It does not end here though! The rest of the design may (possibly..) have originated from an accidental programming bug (our only one ever, surely), where certain spastic button mashes would result in hilariously flinging into the air. Obviously we would not leave this in like this, but we took note that the move actually showed a purpose, and we found a way to integrate it for additional mastery manoeuvres. 

The addition of the [b]Slingshot[/b] move essentially opened up two varieties of complementing other existing movement mechanics; vertically and horizontally. These are not at all required to learn, but they will open new paths to advanced players. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/QhVZ01w.gif[/img]
The vertical [b]Slingshot[/b] provides a boost in an upwards (who would have guessed) direction. To execute it, one must have a certain momentum in order to translate that vertically by combining the [b]Powerslide[/b] and the jump mechanic.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/jwFzEQE.gif[/img]
The horizontal [b]Slingshot[/b] is the combination of using the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/431930/announcements/detail/1674648628976245782][b]Spin[/b][/url], [b]Powerslide[/b] and jump in an almost rhythmical performance, enhancing the forward momentum.

That’s it for this weekend. Next weekend we’ll be back with the [b]Combo[/b] system and how we handled the [b]Camera[/b] in a game that is full of sudden movements and quick turns.

Thanks for reading! Share your thoughts in the comment section below.

Obviously we would not leave this in like this, but we took note that the move actually showed a purpose, and we found a way to integrate it for additional mastery manoeuvres. 

The addition of the [b]Slingshot[/b] move essentially opened up two varieties of complementing other existing movement mechanics; vertically and horizontally. These are not at all required to learn, but they will open new paths to advanced players. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/QhVZ01w.gif[/img]
The vertical [b]Slingshot[/b] provides a boost in an upwards (who would have guessed) direction. To execute it, one must have a certain momentum in order to translate that vertically by combining the [b]Powerslide[/b] and the jump mechanic.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/jwFzEQE.gif[/img]
The horizontal [b]Slingshot[/b] is the combination of using the [url=http://steamcommunity.com/games/431930/announcements/detail/1674648628976245782][b]Spin[/b][/url], [b]Powerslide[/b] and jump in an almost rhythmical performance, enhancing the forward momentum.

That’s it for this weekend. Next weekend we’ll be back with the [b]Combo[/b] system and how we handled the [b]Camera[/b] in a game that is full of sudden movements and quick turns.

Thanks for reading! Share your thoughts in the comment section below.

notes.notes:
The second blog in the series continues showcasing the movement in Kabounce, in this post we’ll discuss the [b]‘Dash’[/b] movement mechanic.
[img]https://i.imgur.com/8GdtOpY.gif[/img]

[h1]Dash Design[/h1]
The [b]Dash[/b] was originally designed shortly after the game jam, back then the ball movement was much trickier and we needed an ability that made it easier to quickly hit a bumper you may have missed. In retrospect, we were obviously designing something to fix a problem, but not actually addressing the problem itself.

Later in development we made the movement smoother, and easier to control. The [b]Dash[/b] became an ability where people wondered, do I really need this? The [b]Dash[/b] was still great for aerial control, but it wasn’t as important anymore. At this stage the dash only featured a left / right direction (using Q / E on keyboard, or LB / RB on a controller).

To make the [b]Dash[/b] great again, we made it a single button press that can be controlled using directional controls. Similar to the spin, this ability now provides a great deal of movement freedom.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/m01x7dN.gif[/img]
Advanced applications of the [b]Dash[/b] allow you to reset the cooldown when you capture a bumper or hoop with the [b]Dash[/b].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/7sgmPZr.gif[/img]
Aside from it being perfect for advanced user to extend air time and allowing you to chain aerial cap, it also works well as a tool to redirect your movement in the air. notes.title: Kabounce Dev Blog - Movement Part 1
notes.notes:
Breaking the silence, we’re going to do a series of blogs each weekend detailing the features of Kabounce until we reach release. Yes, yes, we’ll share our release date very soon too! We’ve just been absolutely slammed with working on improving the game.
 
[img]https://i.imgur.com/u7r9h8q.gif[/img]
Our first series of blogs this weekend we'll focus on a subject which is the very core of our game, the movement.

[h1]Movement Design[/h1]
One subject that has always been front and centre at Stitch Heads while developing Kabounce is: satisfying movement. Tight controls and visceral feedback, your input should feel gratifying and impactful. At the same time the controls in Kabounce should have a skill curve and reward dextrous control and quick reflexes.

Another foremost intent was to keep the game accessible, it should allow someone to quickly pick it up and just play. In that sense you can completely play and enjoy the game with just WASD on keyboard or the left thumb stick on controller. However, Kabounce gives you many more options to improve your momentum and control, and of course impact the game in a meaningful way. Lets look at some of the movement options.

[h1]Advanced Movement:[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/myqIVnp.gif[/img]
The more advanced movement really allows players to keep their momentum up and rapidly change their direction; however, don't get too predictable or you'll get eliminated and your points stolen.

[h1]Basic Movement[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/yvHdu8E.gif[/img]
In comparison, this is the basic movement using just WASD/or left thumb stick on controller (You didn’t see me jump, no. That one time didn’t count):

To get on the topic of some of the more advanced movement, a particular feature I want to highlight in this blog in the movement series is the [b]‘Spin’[/b]. The [b]Spin[/b] essentially gives you control to add ball rotation in specific directions:

[h1]Spinning[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/sHqyRRV.gif[/img]
Side by side comparison of using  a quick [b]Spin[/b] (left) or a regular bounce (right), you can already notice that even a quick [b]Spin[/b] affects your forward momentum.

Other than momentum, use [b]Spinning[/b] to rapidly change direction:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/S2u4CJv.gif[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/QDVtOyw.gif[/img]

Or use the [b]Spin[/b] for vertical movement:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/mMh0fVf.gif[/img]

To use the spin you only have to press a button while in the air. When you have air time, simply press the [b]Spin[/b] button and a direction - as soon as you hit a surface or the ground - you're off!

The [b]Spin[/b] increases in intensity the longer you hold it, to make it more digestible and predictable we’ve ensured there are two ‘steps’ of intensity, and you’ll generally want more air time to build up your spin and reach the second step. In most of the gifs you’ll see one of our devs use it on the fly to intuitively change to their desired direction.

Initially, the [b]Spin[/b] is always something that seems very unusual and unique to new Kabounce players – but once they play around with the Spin and start practicing, they find it easy to learn, and it opens a world of options in Kabounce. 

A lot of the challenges centralise around this core mechanic to not only increase your speed, but adapt your movement. Pixel perfect timings and landings after applying the spin can greatly improve your results of a timed run when doing challenge modes.

We hope you enjoyed, [b]tomorrow (Saturday) is the next blog post, covering the dash![/b] Sunday we’ll reveal the powerslide,a relatively new mechanic.

Thank you for reading! Let us know what you think in the comment section below.
-Tim

notes.title: Kabounce Status Update [July]
notes.notes:
We’ve been working hard towards our release of [url=kabouncegame.com] Kabounce [/url]. We’ve added abilities, multiplayer levels, more customisation content, single player challenges, and more! Check out the video below to see a teaser containing some of this new footage.
[url=https://youtu.be/AuAoPbE7FZI] [img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23793808/83384b70766af9afa66a4e87757b365544e9eab1.gif[/img] [/url]

[h1]DEVELOPMENT UPDATE[/h1]
First, we’re going to start with some bad news.  These last weeks, one of our programmers has had some private issues, and unfortunately he won’t be able to work with us in the foreseeable future ːsteamsadː. We hope he’ll feel better and recover soon! On our release side, this does put us back a little bit.

[h1]RELEASE DATE[/h1]
We viewed mid-2017 as May-August, and had originally anticipated to release late August, up to the 1st of September. With one of our programmers unable to continue, we definitely won't make that and we’re dividing his tasks to our other programmers,they will need to familiarise themselves with his code before they can start on those tasks.

[b]This means it will delay our release slightly, but it won’t affect our capability to release.[/b]

[h1]BETA[/h1]
Before we can open our game as a beta; we need to consider the costs of dedicated servers during a beta period, and consider our remaining tasks that need to be completed. Watch our page for updates on this, or sign up to our newsletter at [url=kabouncegame.com] Kabounce [/url].

[h1]NEW CONTENT[/h1]
We’ve added single player content to Kabounce, challenge mode! Time parkours and aerial platform challenges.
[img] http://i.imgur.com/yqr6W6B.gif [/img]
[img] http://i.imgur.com/GR8R7dt.gif [/img]

We also added more abilities, improved existing abilities, and created more customisation content. You can see some of our customisation in the video at the top the page.

 [h1]FEATURE RECAP[/h1]
[list]
[*]Online up to 4vs4 on dedicated servers
[*]Offline couch co-op, up to 4-player split screen
[*]Experience and cosmetic unlock system
[*]Millions of customisation combinations to make your pinball stand out
[*]Physics based gameplay with multiple uniquely themed pinball arenas
[*]4 diverse and unique abilities to customize your gameplay experience
[*]Electronic music tracks
[*]Single-player challenge mode, set record times and compete on leader boards
[*]Full controller support
[*]In-game group/party support
[/list]

[h1]PRICE[/h1]
We’ve been evaluating our monetization options. We started Kabounce with 3 people outside of college, but it's been a full time job with an entire team for the past year. Originally Kabounce would have peer 2 peer multiplayer, and there weren’t as many features – or as much polish. We're now gearing up for a release with dedicated servers, and matchmaking.

The overhead costs of dedicated servers, the time we’ve invested, and the plan to keep supporting Kabounce after release have caused us to rethink our strategy. We did our research, and received advice from fellow professionals, but also our community on Discord, we are so thankful you have all been worried about the financial future of our studio.

For these reasons, Kabounce is going to cost [b]around $14.99/€14.99 at launch instead of being free to play[/b] this is a guideline, and does not reflect the price in every region. Prices will be adjusted per Steam supported region/currency. 

We hope this will allow us to continue to support dedicated servers and updates post release. For those in the community who have followed and supported us on Discord, or our newsletter, we haven’t forgotten. You’ll receive a discount at launch from us for your continued support and interest in the game.

[h1]DISCORD & SOCIAL MEDIA[/h1]
Don’t forget to join our [url= https://discord.gg/JP2ccZ3][b]Discord channel[/b][/url] for live updates and an easy channel to communicate with the devs!
You can also follow us on Twitter: [url=www.twitter.com/stitchheads] [b]@StitchHeads[/b][/url]
or like us on Facebook: [url=www.facebook.com/StitchHeads][b]facebook/StitchHeads[/b][/url]

I hope this was informative, let us know any questions!

Thanks for reading,
The Stitch Heads team

notes.title: Kabounce December Update!
notes.notes:
[url=https://youtu.be/rBtPZLqi_l4][img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/23793808/9aa01fdb57d94afaf36b0eef31663b0e9b20edbd.gif[/img][/url]

Seasonal greetings and we at Stitch Heads wish you a great Christmas! The long awaited update post is here.

Please click the above image links to watch a video update. Aside from the video update we wanted to share some of the recent developments.

[h1]UPDATE CONTENTS[/h1]
[list]
[*]Steam Store Page, Thumbnails & Release Date
[*]Beta
[*]Gameplay
[*]Multiplayer
[*]Customization
[*]Levels
[*]Mini-games/Challenges
[/list]

[h1]RELEASE DATE[/h1]
On the Steam Store page you can find new screen shots and our update video. As for our release date, we are aiming for mid 2017 as a full release. Around May-June.

We feel this date will both serve our goals in development as the quality we want to provide you at release. The game simply does not conform to our standards right now to release it to the public. As much as we appreciate everyone being anxious to try it, we want to ensure you receive a quality product, instead of another botched product.

[h1]BETA[/h1]
To sign up for the Beta please head to our website and sign up for our news letter at the bottom of the page for a chance to be selected for a Beta.

We'll start Beta testing at the end of January. The first batch of invites will be very small but as we continue to move towards release expect to see a much larger closed Beta for plenty of participants. Beta will be free to participate in.

[h1]GAMEPLAY[/h1]
We've been experimenting with some additional Game Mode settings and how players score points. We've also added a Speed Boost, and looked into a new ability a 'Force Field' which acts as both a defensive and offensive ability. Internal testing has not been too favourable of this ability but you can see it in action in the update video.

In the next update we'll cover the combat and core gameplay updates we have been making. Currently it can use more polish before we announce any gameplay changes publicly.

[h1]MULTIPLAYER[/h1]
We have been updating the multiplayer backend of our code. While this is not something tangible that we can show, it is there. These updates should provide more stability, and allow us to move forward with a more robust network system.

We are also in talks with a third party provider and are looking into having full dedicated server support at launch for you to enjoy. Current systems were reliant on players to host; however, in a competitive multiplayer game we realized this may not give use the quality we are looking for.

Kabounce now also features offline - and online - split screen support with 2-player, 3-player, and 4-player split screen. Complimented with bots this should allow players to even enjoy Kabounce on the couch in the company of friends!

[h1]CUSTOMIZATION[/h1]
Please refer to the video to see some of the new content options and our more robust pinball customization system in action! Our current customization system works as follows:

[list]
[*]Select a [b]base pinball[/b]
[*]Add [b]modifications[/b]
[*]Compliment it with [b]accessories[/b] (top, middle, and bottom slots)
[*]and add a [b]pinball trail[/b] effect
[/list]

[h1]LEVELS[/h1]
We're working on some completely new levels and have finished a few visual styles or themes in the Kabounce neon-style. Current themes:
[list]
[*]Arena
[*]Asian Temple
[*]Under Water City
[/list]
The Under Water City is still being worked on, the Arena and Asian Temple theme are close to being completely final.

[h1]MINI-GAMES/CHALLENGES[/h1]
We will soon start working on mini-game like challenges for players to enjoy as a single player experience.

The idea is that these single player challenges will provide offline as well as leaderboards competitiveness. Pinball is originally a single player experience, therefore we would also like to cater to single player and pinball enthusiast looking for a different experience of pinball.

Thanks! We hope you enjoyed this update, let us know what you think or if you have any questions.

Enjoy the holidays!

-Tim

To sign up for the Beta please head to our website and sign up for our news letter at the bottom of the page for a chance to be selected for a Beta.

We'll start Beta testing at the end of January. The first batch of invites will be very small but as we continue to move towards release expect to see a much larger closed Beta for plenty of participants. Beta will be free to participate in.

[h1]GAMEPLAY[/h1]
We've been experimenting with some additional Game Mode settings and how players score points. We've also added a Speed Boost, and looked into a new ability a 'Force Field' which acts as both a defensive and offensive ability. Internal testing has not been too favourable of this ability but you can see it in action in the update video.

In the next update we'll cover the combat and core gameplay updates we have been making. Currently it can use more polish before we announce any gameplay changes publicly.

[h1]MULTIPLAYER[/h1]
We have been updating the multiplayer backend of our code. While this is not something tangible that we can show, it is there. These updates should provide more stability, and allow us to move forward with a more robust network system.

We are also in talks with a third party provider and are looking into having full dedicated server support at launch for you to enjoy. Current systems were reliant on players to host; however, in a competitive multiplayer game we realized this may not give use the quality we are looking for.

Kabounce now also features offline - and online - split screen support with 2-player, 3-player, and 4-player split screen. Complimented with bots this should allow players to even enjoy Kabounce on the couch in the company of friends!
